_spec.rule: Data, risk, solver and experiment settings are read from this file via load_params_v18.py; library functions in qopt/ carry defaults that the scripts always override with these values. Fixed memory caps in the code: exact enumeration up to 24 items, joint full-space distributions up to 5,000,000 states.
_spec.sensitivity_policy: Fields named 'sensitivity*' declare plausible ranges for the reader. The scripts run these sensitivities: Student-t copula and sigma 0.04 with epsilon 0.01 (Section 3.5, validation_cases), stress scenarios S1-S5 (3.4), weight sweep (3.6), CVaR alpha 1 (Benchmark B, --alpha 1). All other sensitivity values are declared only.

blocks._note: Each qubit = one contracted block of one route. Block size b_m = ceil(D_m / k_req_m / unit_m) * unit_m. In the optimisation objective, cost and emissions are charged on contracted tonnes. Out-of-sample evaluation (Section 3.5) charges emissions on delivered tonnes and cost with the cost-shock multiplier.
blocks.label: A
blocks.reason: Block sizes follow one rule tied to sourced demand and transport units, so a buffer above demand is a real decision. Pool sizes are the smallest that make the 95% joint chance constraint feasible with spare choices left (16 feasible count vectors under the base risk settings; printed by load_params_v18.py).

objective.normalisation: C_ref, E_ref, R_ref = values with all blocks selected (D). f = w_cost*Cost/C_ref + w_emit*Emis/E_ref + w_risk*Risk/R_ref.

risk_term.definition: Risk(x) = sum over materials m of Var_scenarios(sum_{i in m} b_i x_i F_route(i)) / D_m^2 = x^T Q x, Q_ij = Cov(b_i F_i, b_j F_j)/D_m^2 for i,j in the same material, 0 across materials
risk_term.scenarios: calibration scenarios of the run (same copula family and severity)
risk_term.label: A
risk_term.reason: supply-volatility term from the copula-GPD scenarios; makes the optimisation non-trivial and puts the risk model inside the objective

capacity_shock.reason_level: A: one disruption (port, rail line, road corridor) hits every block of the route alike
capacity_shock.label: A

cost_shock.label: A
cost_shock.source: assumption: unsourced; applied to cost only
cost_shock.use: evaluation of expected cost and regret only
cost_shock.dependence: same copula draw as capacity_shock (comonotone within a route)

copula.label: A
copula.source: assumption: 0.7 between routes of the same material; 0 across materials (sensitivity 0.3)

chance_constraint.form: joint over coal, ore, scrap: P(sum of delivered >= D_m for all m) >= 1 - epsilon
chance_constraint.label: A
chance_constraint.reason: Under the base shock severity, epsilon = 0.01 is infeasible even with all 18 blocks (all-on calibration violation 0.032, printed by load_params_v18.py); 0.05 is the tightest round value that is feasible with choices left.

calibration.rule: over grid values <= epsilon, use the largest epsilon_cal whose safe-count optimum is certified on validation; if none, report the case as not certifiable. The exact SAA optimum (no count buffer) is reported alongside for comparison.

validation.certify: one-sided Clopper-Pearson upper bound (confidence statistics.confidence) on the violation rate <= epsilon

safe_count_rule.rule: Blocks within a route are identical, so the buffered demand constraint is a count constraint per material: count_m(x) >= k_m. For a given epsilon_cal, k is 'safe' if every route-count vector whose material counts are >= k has calibration violation <= epsilon_cal. Among safe k, choose the one whose best (exact) objective is lowest; ties -> smallest total k.
safe_count_rule.label: A

tost_margin_objective.label: A
tost_margin_objective.reason: pre-specified equivalence margin in normalised-objective units

validation_cases.role: tighter epsilon; feasible only with the milder severity (sensitivity_epsilon)

chance_constraint.validation_cases_note: sigma null = capacity_shock.sigma; nu used only for student_t

stress_scenarios.label: A (illustrative)
stress_scenarios.check: report for every scenario whether the exact optimum moves and whether a certified plan exists

list.description: R4 available blocks 3 -> 2 (capacity 39,000 -> 26,000 t/month, -33%). A 50% cut (19,500 t) is not representable with 13,000 t blocks; 2 blocks is the nearest level that leaves a certified plan (1 block leaves a single feasible plan).

methods.label: A

common.init_p1: uniform: gamma in pi*init_gamma_range_over_pi, beta in pi*init_beta_range_over_pi (M1-M4); M5 uses methods.M5.init_halfwidth
common.depth_schedule: INTERP (Zhou et al. 2020) from p to p+1 within one seed chain
common.shot_seed_rule: sampling seed for the final shots = shot_seed_stride * run seed + p
common.optimizer_options: scipy.optimize.minimize(method='COBYLA') with scipy defaults except maxiter; COBYLA's path can differ slightly between scipy versions, which are recorded in every summary.json

methods.headline: M1
methods.headline_note: M1 is the proposed method; M2 is its single-angle (minimal-parameter) variant. Case-study scripts (3.4-3.6) use the headline method.

M1.name: MPSX-QAOA (proposed): multi-angle, one beta per XY edge
M1.mixer: XY ring per material register incl. slack qubits, one angle per edge

M2.name: MPSX-QAOA, single-angle variant (one beta per register)
M2.mixer: XY ring per material register incl. slack qubits
M2.initial_state: Dicke state per register (uniform over weight = n_items_in_group)

M3.name: Standard QAOA, X mixer, quadratic penalty with binary slack
M3.constraint: penalty: A * M * sum_g (count_g - k_g - s_g)^2

M4.name: QAOA with unbalanced penalisation (Montanez-Barrera et al. 2024)
M4.constraint: penalty: M * sum_g (-lambda1*h_g + lambda2*h_g^2), h_g = count_g - k_g

M5.name: Multi-angle particle-conserving ansatz (MA-PC), adapted to three materials
M5.structure: free RZ per item qubit, free RZZ per item pair with nonzero risk coupling, XY chain over items (shared angle RXX/RYY), XY between every slack and every item; one global register of weight N_items; S = N_items - sum(k) slack qubits
M5.init_p1: uniform [-init_halfwidth, init_halfwidth] (as in the original ansatz design)
M5.constraint: global count structural; per-material deficit penalised in the CVaR energy: A * M * sum_g deficit_g^2

tuning.rule: penalty parameters of M3/M4 maximise mean P(optimum) over tune_seeds (seed_offset + 0 .. tune_seeds-1, disjoint from evaluation seeds) at depth tune_p (profile). Synthetic suite: on n_tuning_instances held-out instances (seeds disjoint from evaluation instances). Steel case: on the steel instance itself (single instance). Chosen values are written to the results.

methods.penalty_scale: M = max_i (lin_i + W_ii + 2 sum_j |W_ij|): largest single-item contribution to f; all penalties are in units of M

classical.exact: enumeration of all 2^N item bitstrings (ground truth)
classical.milp: PuLP/CBC on the McCormick linearisation of the QUBO (MILP); optional if pulp is installed; checked against enumeration
classical.greedy: per material, add the item with the smallest marginal objective until count = k_g

seeds.rule: heuristic seeds start .. start + profile seeds - 1

quick.note: quick: M3/M4 run on the synthetic suite only (18-20 qubit full-space baselines are slow on steel); paper profile runs all five on steel

paper.note: paper: 20 instances x 3 sizes, 10 seeds, p<=4 (M3 not run at [5,5,5], see synthetic_suite.method_exclusions); the suite resumes after a disconnect

synthetic_suite.label: synthetic (not steel data)
synthetic_suite.k_rule: k_g uniform integer in [max(1, n_g - k_spread), n_g - 1]
synthetic_suite.risk: Q_g = B B^T / n_g with B ~ N(0,1) (n_g x n_g), within group only

method_exclusions.reason: compute budget: full-space simulation of M3 at this size needs up to 21 qubits (about 30 h of the paper-profile run on a 2-vCPU Colab runtime); M3 is reported at [3,3,3] and [4,4,4]

synthetic_suite.seed_rule: evaluation instance j of size index s: base_seed + size_seed_stride*s + j (j < tuning_seed_offset); tuning instance j: base_seed + size_seed_stride*s + tuning_seed_offset + j (disjoint from evaluation instances)
synthetic_suite.capacity_rule: A method is not run on an instance whose simulation exceeds its stated cap (M3/M4: full_space_qubit_cap qubits; M5: methods.M5.subspace_dim_cap register states, dimension C(N+S, N)). Such instances are recorded in instances.csv (column skipped) and paired tests use only instances where both methods ran.

gradient_variance.derivative: central finite difference with step fd_step on up to grad_k_max sampled last-layer mixer angles; energy rescaled to [0,1] by the method's own range; mean of per-angle variances reported
gradient_variance.init_seed_rule: initialisation seed = init_seed_stride * size index + p
gradient_variance.inits_note: each initialisation draws every angle uniformly from the stated interval (radians)

dla.note: illustrative small cases only; M3 needs >= 6 qubits (64-dim) even for [2,2] and is skipped
dla.instance_rule: Q_g = B B^T / n_g with B ~ N(0,1); cost and emissions uniform in cost_emis_range; k_g = n_g - k_offset_below_n

depth_sweep.rule: p values above the profile p_max are not run

noise.label: A (simulated sensitivity scenario, not a hardware calibration)
noise.method: Monte Carlo Pauli trajectories on the full statevector; readout flips at sampling
noise.post_selection: M1, M2: keep shots whose register Hamming weights are conserved

penalty_params.note: fixed for the noise study (not tuned)

noise.training: each method trained noiselessly on profile seeds; the seed with the highest noiseless P(optimum) is evaluated under noise
noise.rule: p2 = 0 is the fully noiseless reference (p1 = 0, no readout flips)

regression_targets._note: Loader must reproduce manuscript Tables 1 and 2 within tolerance.

statistics.holm: Holm correction over all rows of each paired-test table
statistics.intervals: Clopper-Pearson one-sided upper bound for violation rates; Wilson interval for survival; percentile bootstrap for medians

qiskit.label: A
qiskit.purpose: (1) cross-validate saved trained circuits of the numpy engine against Qiskit statevectors; (2) report transpiled circuit resources; (3) simulated noise with the Qiskit Aer noise model for Section 3.3

cross_validation.group: source x size x method x depth p
cross_validation.compare: P(optimum) and P(feasible) from exact probabilities at the saved trained angles

resources.note: layers only (state preparation excluded and stated); gate structure does not depend on the nonzero angle or penalty values
resources.optimization_level_rule: must be 0 or 1 (higher levels may permute qubits; enforced in code)

aer_noise.simulator: qiskit_aer.AerSimulator(method='statevector'): one trajectory per shot, noise on transpiled native gates
aer_noise.parameter_rule: Aer depolarizing_error takes the depolarizing parameter lambda; it is set to lambda = p * d^2 / (d^2 - 1) so that p is the probability of a non-identity Pauli error, as in noise.p1_depolarising / p2_depolarising_sweep
aer_noise.readout: symmetric flip probability noise.readout_flip on every qubit
aer_noise.state_preparation: ideal (initialize, noiseless), as in the trajectory simulation
aer_noise.model_difference: trajectory model (Section 3.3): one error per logical two-qubit operation (RZZ, XY edge) and p1 after RZ/RX; Aer: p2 per native CX (RZZ ~ 2 CX, XY edge ~ 4 CX) and p1 per sx/x
